headline: Five things moved since the August 31 briefing. Everything else on the register is unchanged and is listed at the foot without being repeated.
scope: Built from the public record alone: filings accepted by EDGAR, press releases, and the company's own pages, read on September 15, 2026. No internal source of any kind.

items.headline: The window to nominate a director for the 2026 annual meeting shut on Sunday, and the meeting date is still not public

what_happened.text: The bylaw window for stockholder proposals and director nominations at the 2026 annual meeting shut at the close of business on Sunday, September 13. It had opened on August 14.

what_changed.text: At the last briefing it was open with thirteen days to run. It is shut, and nothing has been filed since to announce the date of the meeting.

why_it_matters.text: The same paragraph reopens it for ten days after a public announcement if the meeting falls more than 30 days before, or more than 60 days after, December 12. The meeting date, still unset, is what decides whether nominations are shut. Whether a submission on Monday the 14th would count against a Sunday deadline is a question for counsel.

who_owns_it.text: The bylaws name the Secretary of the Company. Scott Bartley has held that office, with Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, since October 27, 2025.

what_is_late.text: Nothing. A window shut on its own terms, and the June 30 deadline for proposals printed in the proxy passed on schedule.

decision_required.text: Set the date of the 2026 annual meeting. That one choice settles this window, the proxy calendar and item five.

next_step.text: Next board agenda. Ask the Secretary to confirm on the record what came in between August 14 and September 13.

items.headline: The annual report for the year ended June 30 is due in thirteen days, on Monday September 28

what_happened.text: The fiscal year ended June 30. As a non-accelerated filer and a smaller reporting company, the annual report is due ninety days later: Monday, September 28.

what_changed.text: Twenty eight days remained at the last briefing. Thirteen remain. Nothing filed in the interval touches the report.

why_it_matters.text: It is the first annual report drafted after the June board approval of a sale process for 1st Detect and the August replacement of the equity program. Last year the results release came out the day before the report, so that date is already inside the window.

who_owns_it.text: The Interim Chief Financial Officer, with RBSM LLP, ratified by stockholders as auditor for this year.

what_is_late.text: Nothing is late. Last year's report was filed on the eighty eighth day.

decision_required.text: Fix the results release date, and name who reviews the sale process and equity program language before signature.

next_step.text: Lock the calendar this week. Item three should be settled before the report is signed, not after.

items.headline: Seven amended insider reports were filed in thirteen minutes on September 8, one of them correcting a report from March 2024
answers: WHAT CHANGED IN THE LAST 24 HOURS

what_happened.text: EDGAR indexes seven Forms 4/A under September 8, accepted between 21:02 and 21:15 Eastern, amending reports for five insiders. One corrects a report originally filed on March 18, 2024.

what_changed.text: None of it existed on August 31. One amended report was a week old: the Form 4 filed September 1 carries a date of earliest transaction of December 13, 2024, while the award it reports is dated September 1, 2026. The amendment restates that date.

why_it_matters.text: A batch across five insiders reaching back to March 2024 reads as the output of a review of past filings rather than one clerical fix. This briefing sees the output on EDGAR, not the review, so that is offered as a reading. The calendar is not a reading: the proxy must name every insider whose report was late during the year, and last year's named three.

who_owns_it.text: The Corporate Secretary, with securities counsel. The five are four directors and the Chief Operating Officer.

what_is_late.text: The amendments are not themselves a finding of lateness. But the annual report is due September 28, the proxy follows it, and that paragraph is drafted from this material.

decision_required.text: Ask counsel, before the annual report is signed, for the list of fiscal 2026 reports filed after their due date and for what triggered the batch.

next_step.text: One request to counsel this week. It costs an email and settles a paragraph proxy advisers read closely.

items.new_since_previous: the company's own board page was read on September 15 and still shows six directors, sixty one days after the seventh was appointed
items.headline: Your public record disagrees with itself about the size of your board, in three places
answers: WHAT SHOULD I KNOW THAT NOBODY HAS DIRECTLY TOLD ME

what_happened.text: Item 5.02 of the Form 8-K of July 22 says the Board went from six directors to seven. The press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to that same filing says five to six. The Executive Team page shows the Chairman and five directors, six names.

what_changed.text: The contradiction inside the July 22 filing was in the last briefing. New is the reconciliation: the board page, read on September 15, is sixty one days behind the July 16 board action. The same page lists no Chief Financial Officer, while an Interim Chief Financial Officer has been in office since October 27, 2025.

why_it_matters.text: Six directors stood for election on December 12, 2025, so the Item 5.02 figure is the one that agrees with the record. The press release is the document that travels: data vendors and proxy advisers read it first, and a counterparty checks the website second. The 2026 proxy will have to state one number, with seven names under it.

who_owns_it.text: The Corporate Secretary. The board that acted in July now includes a director whose career is investor relations, and his is the name missing from the page.

what_is_late.text: No filing is late. The Form 8-K went in four business days after the board acted. The company's own pages are behind, by sixty one days on the board and three hundred and twenty three on the finance seat.

decision_required.text: Whether the July 22 release is corrected, and who owns the board page and the newsroom.

next_step.text: One pass over the two pages before the proxy is drafted. Then one rule: no release goes out unread against the filing it is attached to.

items.new_since_previous: item one put the annual meeting date in play, and every extension of this agreement so far has been signed on the day of that meeting
items.headline: The rights plan reaches its expiration on December 20, and the decision has travelled with the annual meeting every year since 2023

what_happened.text: Amendment No. 3, entered into December 12, 2025, extends the Final Expiration Date to 5:00 P.M. New York City time on December 20, 2026. Ninety six days out.

what_changed.text: Nothing about the agreement. It is repeated on purpose: its context changed when the nomination window shut and put the meeting date in play.

why_it_matters.text: The three amendments were signed December 18, 2023, December 12, 2024 and December 12, 2025, the last on the day of the annual meeting. Three points are a habit, not a rule, but they put this decision and the meeting date on one agenda.

who_owns_it.text: The Board of Directors, with Equiniti Trust Company as rights agent.

what_is_late.text: Nothing. Ninety six days remain, and each of the last three extensions was signed within nine days of the expiration.

decision_required.text: Extend a fourth time, redeem, or let it reach the Final Expiration Date.

next_step.text: Same board agenda as item one. If the meeting moves out of December, this date does not move with it.

alerts.rule: a current report carrying a board decision about a subsidiary
alerts.text: the board approved management to engage in a sale process for 1st Detect, announced the same morning.

alerts.rule: a change to an active equity program, accepted after the close
alerts.text: a $50 million prospectus supplement replaced the June program, and a second filing terminated it, twenty six minutes apart.

alerts.rule: three or more amended insider reports accepted inside one hour
alerts.text: seven Forms 4/A for five insiders, one of them correcting a report from March 2024.

carried.text: The $50 million prospectus supplement of August 19 stands, after approximately $7.9 million of gross proceeds under the June program.
The sale process for 1st Detect, approved by the board on June 16, has had no disclosed update.
The NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services 2 Phase 1 proposal, submitted June 30, has no disclosed decision date.
The quarterly report for the period ended March 31 was amended on August 6 to correct the Series D conversion share count.
Matthew Kreps joined the board on July 16 and had not been assigned to a committee as of July 22.
